issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise PerformanceWarning` is dead code revealing undecided control flow.
issues.detail: The `break` immediately following `raise` is unreachable. This indicates the author was undecided between warn-and-continue versus fail-fast. Pick one posture and delete the other. Dead code in a 20-line validation patch is a red flag that the loop's postcondition was never stated.

issues.description: Raising `PerformanceWarning` conflates a warning class with a fatal exception.
issues.detail: `PerformanceWarning` is by name and convention a Warning subclass intended for `warnings.warn`, not `raise`. Using it as a fatal exception is a category error — the name lies about behavior. The test then cements this with `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning)`. Either rename to an Error class and raise, or call `warnings.warn` and let the user proceed.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` math is incoherent; `max(1, dtype.itemsize)` papers over a non-case.
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` guards against zero itemsize, but numpy itemsize is always >=1 for real dtypes. Either the guard is dead or it hides unhandled object/structured dtypes. Also, the relation between this scalar and the `array.chunk-size` config advised to the user is not linear. State the precondition; don't invent a number.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` is precedence-brittle; write `% zw != 0`.
issues.detail: Python parses this correctly only by accident of operator precedence. A reader must simulate the parser to verify the guard. Rewrite as `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` — one operator, obvious intent. Code requiring precedence recall for a guard clause wastes maintainer time for zero benefit.

issues.description: Only `dw[0]` is checked; verdict is rendered for the whole axis without justification.
issues.detail: The loop inspects only the first dask chunk per axis, but `normalize_chunks("auto", ...)` can produce a smaller tail chunk whose divisibility is never checked. State the invariant: must all chunks on the axis be divisible by `zw`, or only the nominal? Then verify what is stated. A comment-free heuristic will silently miss misalignment.

issues.description: PR ships `raise` while description asks whether raising is correct — policy undecided.
issues.detail: The author openly asks whether an exception is appropriate when config competes with shard shape, yet the diff already raises, the docstring says "performance warning," and the message warns of "data loss" risk. Three stories. Decide the contract before merge and make code, tests, and message agree.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously rejects this diff as not ready. The core idea — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `auto_chunks` produces shard-aligned chunks — has merit, but the validation block is unreasoned: a `raise` followed by an unreachable `break`, a Warning class raised as a fatal exception (and a test that cements the confusion), and a `safe_chunk_size` calculation guarded by a meaningless `max(1, itemsize)`. The divisibility check inspects only the first chunk per axis, uses brittle precedence (`not x % y == 0`), and the PR description itself admits the policy is undecided. NEEDS-WORK: pick warn-or-raise, name the class accordingly, fix the size math, check all chunks, and align code, tests, message, and docstring on one contract.
